A band gap Δ = 1.18 eV in the ground-state electronic structure
A sudden drop in activation energy at T ∼ 240 K from Ea ∼ 1 eV in the low-temperature phase to Ea ∼ 0.3 eV at room temperature

records.text: Paper card. System: (Gd0.2Nd0.2La0.2Sm0.2Y0.2)CoO3. Processing: modified coprecipitation hydrothermal method with quenching in liquid nitrogen, 72 h at 150 °C under autogenous pressure, then heated up to 1200 °C and kept at this temperature for 2 h in an air atmosphere. Test conditions: temperature range from 3 up to 300 K, magnetic field of 100 mT, temperature range from 225 up to 450 K. Findings: The compound exhibits weak ferromagnetism at T ≤ 10 K; Signatures of antiferromagnetic correlations in the paramagnetic phase; A band gap Δ = 1.18 eV in the ground-state electronic structure; A sudden drop in activation energy at T ∼ 240 K from Ea ∼ 1 eV in the low-temperature phase to Ea ∼ 0.3 eV at room temperature; The configuration entropy calculated using eq 1 is equal to 1.61R (0.0134 kJ·mol–1·K–1); The orthorhombic perovskite structure with small (less than 4%) precipitation of the RE2O3 phase; The semiconductor-to-semiconductor transition is related to the evolution of the electronic structure related to structural distortion. Mechanism: The high configuration entropy of the A-site cations is likely responsible for good accommodation of the deformation of CoO6 octahedra by the lattice and thus a lack of sudden structural phase transitions. Future work: Fine tuning of cationic stoichiometry in high-entropy cobalt oxides may be used to optimize the value of activation energy and temperature of phase transition in a wide range required by the different applications of perovskite cobalt oxides. Quote: "High-Entropy Perovskites as Multifunctional Metal Oxide Semiconductors"
